Not Your Typical Bowl of Pho
Jun 2026 • Solo
First, I got the Nem Vuong. It was a bit difficult to bite and chew, and some of the ingredients would get stuck between my teeth with every bite. While it had a savory aroma, the flavor itself was milder than expected and did not deliver the same savory impact that the smell suggested. Next, I tried the Lion's Mane Pho. The ingredients felt high quality, and the dish gave off an almost royal feeling, as if it were a bowl of pho made for kings rather than everyday diners. The broth tasted different from a traditional pho, offering a unique flavor that set it apart from the versions found elsewhere. The noodles were cooked perfectly, and although there were only a few pieces of lion's mane mushroom, they still managed to stand out as one of the highlights of the dish. My only criticism for this dish is that the restaurant served two large slabs of tofu instead of slicing them into smaller pieces, which would have made the bowl easier to enjoy. If you're expecting a classic bowl of Vietnamese pho, this is not it. Instead, think of it as a refined interpretation. I also ordered the Vi Que Milk Tea, which was excellent. I wish it had been served in a larger glass. Lastly, I really appreciated the restaurant's design.

Michelin Recognition. Fully Deserved.
Mar 2026 • Couples
Vi Que Kitchen lives up to every bit of its acclaim. We visited twice — once for an early dinner, once for lunch — and it delivered both times.

At dinner we arrived at 4:30pm and settled in during happy hour, which meant buy-one-get-one drinks: two beers for my husband, two very well-made cosmos for me. A very good start. The food was extraordinary. I had the lion's mane mushroom pho, and we shared a braised mushroom and ginger dish that was “melt in your mouth” wonderful. My husband ordered the bánh xèo — an enormous, theatrical plate with a sizzling pancake surrounded by towers of fresh lettuce and herbs. Everything was excellent.

We came back for lunch the next day. I wanted to try something new — the entire menu is tempting — but the previous day's dishes were simply too good to pass up. I ordered the same without a moment of regret. My husband went for the fried rice, which was exactly what his stomach needed that day — perhaps not the most vibrant choice on the menu, but with the juice from the braised mushroom and ginger, it was tasty.

If I lived nearby, I'd be back every day working my way through the menu, starting with the banh mi. And at these prices, that wouldn't be hard to justify.

My only suggestion is that the banana desert was beautiful, but needed to be a little bit sweeter for my taste.

Don't miss this one. Reservations are typically required for dinner, but we got in for both visits — early dinner and lunch — without them. Go early if you want to walk in.

For vegans and non vegans worth it
Dec 2025 • Couples
To be honest not many out of the 47 michelin guide Restaurants in saigon are worth it. So its quite refreshing if you find a place thats worth your while.

The restaurant sits in a quiet street with many parking spots. When approaching the place the staff opens the door to direct you to your table. That welcoming and incredibly fast service continues throughout the dining experience. When a chopstick well it was replaced in a matter of seconds before we could even adress the issue.

The restaurant exclusively serves vegan food. We had bun nam nuong with springrolls and a very special lionsmane pho. The soup had a beautiful combination auf different mushrooms and herbs and sprices. The herbs and spices can be ordered fresh or sauteed. The broth although vegan felt so richtig that you wouldnt believe that no bones were used.

A great experience.
